title: Algorithmic Fairness Datasets: the Story so Far

bias_targets.methodology: Surveying and documenting datasets (e.g., Winogender, Adult, CelebA) used to evaluate gender fairness across tasks like classification, coreference resolution, and representation learning.

Surveying datasets (e.g., COMPAS, FairFace, BOLD) used to measure performance disparities and representation across racial and ethnic groups in risk assessment, facial recognition, and language modeling.
Cataloging datasets (e.g., Adience, Adult, German Credit) that include age as a sensitive attribute to audit predictive models for age-related accuracy disparities and fairness.
Analyzing tabular datasets (e.g., German Credit, HMDA, Adult) used to assess fairness, disparate impact, and resource allocation in credit scoring, loan approvals, and income prediction.
Identifying text and speech datasets (e.g., TwitterAAE, YouTube Dialect Accuracy) designed to evaluate model robustness and speech recognition accuracy across different regional dialects.
Documenting NLP and vision datasets (e.g., BOLD, iEAT) created to evaluate stereotypical associations and performance disparities across different religious identities.
Reviewing datasets (e.g., Civil Comments, iEAT) that track sexual orientation to evaluate unintended bias in toxicity classification and learned representations.
Surveying datasets (e.g., Civil Comments, iEAT) that include disability status to audit algorithmic fairness and representation in automated text moderation and computer vision.
Documenting datasets (e.g., Twitter Political Searches, BOLD) used to measure bias in search engine rankings and language models regarding political leaning.
Cataloging datasets (e.g., CVs from Singapore) used to evaluate nationality and geographic origin bias in automated hiring and ranking systems.
